question: How great a material wealth is declared insufficient compared to this teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels is imagined
Someone may possess such an accumulation
This wealth is set up as a comparison
inference: Even one who could amass an ocean filled with jewels lacks a comparable treasure
uncertainties: The form akretuṃ is irregular and the comparison is completed in the next verse
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels.
